To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
personal contractual interactions with individual researchers play a major role in knowledge transfer between universities and firms.

1) the governance of university industry knowledge flows is a complex phenomenon involving multiple actors and different governance modes; 2) the governance modes of university-industry interactions are complementary, and both are relevant for the knowledge transfer process; 3) the governance of knowledge flows from university to industry involves both the institutional mode (mediated by the university) and the personal contractual mode (mediated through formal and binding contractual arrangements between firms and individual researchers).

personal contractual arrangements between firms and individual researchers are the dominant form of governance for university industry knowledge transfer and that both governance modes have different implications for firms’ strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the governance of the university industry interactions, with the aim to provide new evidence on the role of different governance modes in the context of open innovation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the institutional governance mode is used by large firms with strong R&D departments, while the personal contractual governance mode is more appropriate for small firms that have not developed a dedicated R&D department.
firms should not be forced to choose between one governance mode or the other, but rather should be encouraged to use both.
both modes of governance are necessary to capture all the different types of university industry interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

firms are more likely to use the institutional governance mode when they have a high level of internal R&D and when they are involved in vertical integration of R&D activities, while they are more likely to choose the personal contractual governance mode when they engage in open innovation activities and have a high level or external technology.

firms use different governance modes to interact with universities and that the choice of governance mode is related to firm characteristics and strategies, as well as to the characteristics and strategies adopted by the universities.
the institutional mode is used by firms that are more likely to have an internal R&D capability, whereas personal contractual agreements are used by firms that do not possess such capability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of governance mode is a strategic one and should be taken into account in the design of policies aimed at fostering university industry interactions.
firms’ decision to use a specific governance mode is not random but is rather driven by the firms’ characteristics and the specific nature of the knowledge transfer process.
both institutional and personal contractual modes of governance are important and complementary in the university industry knowledge transfer process.
